content.title: About
content.content: Meat, NFS (Non‑Fatty Substance) is a high‑quality meat product that has had almost all fat and connective tissue removed. The product retains the natural flavor and nutrients of meat while offering dramatically reduced calories and fat content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The NFS process reduces fat content to less than 1 % without losing protein.
It is widely used in diet plans and sports nutrition.
NFS meat retains most B‑vitamins and minerals found in whole meat.
The technology relies on vacuum separation followed by steam treatment.
NFS meat has a longer shelf life compared with fresh meat.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: A serving provides about 20 g of protein, essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Fat content is under 1 %, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12, B6 and niacin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides iron, zinc and selenium, important for immunity and blood formation.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: Approximately 100 kcal per 100 g, helpful for weight management.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to meat proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The product is often salted for preservation; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Cooking safety
items.content: Cook to an internal temperature of 71 °C to prevent food‑borne illnesses.

items.title: Not suitable for vegetarians or vegans

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: NFS meat can be sautéed, baked, boiled, or steamed. It is commonly added to salads, soups, noodle dishes, and protein shakes. Its low‑fat nature allows quick cooking without excess oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C in an airtight package for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze at ‑18 °C, where it remains good for up to 6 months. Thaw in the fridge, not at room temperature.

mushrooms-fresh-cooked-no-added-fat.title: Mushrooms, fresh, cooked without added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Mushrooms are edible fruiting bodies of fungi that grow in the wild and are cultivated on farms. Fresh mushrooms cooked without added fat (e.g., steamed, baked, or boiled) retain most of their nutrients and have a mild, slightly earthy flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mushrooms are not plants; they belong to their own kingdom – Fungi.
More than 10,000 edible mushroom species exist, including button, oyster, honey, and shiitake.
Mushrooms can produce vitamin D when exposed to ultraviolet light.
Unlike most vegetables, mushrooms are very low in carbohydrates and contain virtually no sugar.
Mushrooms are a natural source of beta‑glucans – fibers that support the immune system.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Mushrooms contain more protein per gram than most vegetables, making them a good plant‑based protein source.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: 100 g of fresh mushrooms provide about 22 kcal, ideal for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Mushrooms supply niacin, riboflavin, pyridoxine, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contain minerals
items.content: Mushrooms provide potassium, selenium, copper, and iron, important for heart and immune function.

items.title: Support gut microbiota
items.content: Beta‑glucans and other fibers in mushrooms promote the growth of beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to certain mushroom varieties.

items.title: Toxic species
items.content: Foraging wild mushrooms without expert identification can lead to poisoning from toxic varieties.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Mushrooms contain purines, so people with gout should limit their intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mushrooms can be eaten raw in salads, but are most often steamed, baked, sautéed, or boiled without added oil. Slice them for soups, stews, omelets, or use as a meat substitute in vegetarian dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh mushrooms in the refrigerator in a paper bag or breathable container so they can “breathe.” Use them within 3–5 days. For longer storage, blanch and freeze them.
